prompt: A narrow London by-street of shop fronts on a Sunday morning. Along the left side a row of shop fronts runs into the distance: freshly painted green and cream shutters, polished brass rails and brass door plates, tall plate-glass windows with furled awnings above them. The pavement is clean grey flagstone edged with a granite kerb; the roadway is swept dark cobbles. Along the right side stand dingy soot-blackened brick houses with dull grimy windows. A cast-iron gas lamp post stands at the kerb in the middle distance. Grey daylight falls in from the upper left over the rooftops, and the shutters throw black shadow bars across the flagstones. Raking grey daylight from the LEFT, deep shadow.

A street corner in a sleeping London quarter at three in the morning. Two streets meet at a right angle: a long straight street running away from the near left, and a cross street coming down from the right. Terraced brick houses with shuttered windows and dark doorways line both streets, their front steps edged with black iron railings. Cast-iron gas lamps burn at even intervals along both kerbs, each throwing a pool of yellow light on frosted cobbles. A tall lamp post stands at the corner kerb itself. The yellow gaslight falls from the corner lamp on the right, throwing long black shadows from the railings across the pavement; above the rooftops the sky is coal black.

A small London by-street at night, its row of shop fronts closed behind freshly painted shutters with polished brass rails. Two doors from the corner the row breaks at the entry of a court, and there a two-storey block thrusts its gable forward: a blind upper wall of discoloured plaster above a single blistered, stained door set in a shallow recess with three worn stone steps. A gas lamp on the kerb throws yellow light from the left across the door and the steps, casting black shadows into the recess at the right.
